exposure: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) use in pregnancy (late-pregnancy and midpregnancy exposure)
Selective serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs) use in pregnancy (late-pregnancy and midpregnancy exposure)
cohort: The study included 225,973 women with 322,224 pregnancies in British Columbia, Canada, between 2002 and 2011.
finding: Serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (SNRI) exposure in late pregnancy was associated with a 1.6-to 1.9-fold increased risk of postpartum hemorrhage, while selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) use in the final month of pregnancy showed a significant relationship only under specific adjustments.
